subject: Transportation Systems
title: AIS: Tracking Every Ship
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: AIS: Tracking Every Ship.

hook.text: Every large ship broadcasts its identity, position, speed, and heading every few seconds via radio.

buildup.text: The Automatic Identification System is mandatory for all vessels over 300 tons on international voyages.

discovery.text: AIS signals are picked up by coastal stations and satellites, creating a live map of global shipping.

twist.text: Some ships turn off AIS to hide—smugglers, sanction violators, and illegal fishing operations.

climax.text: Analysts now use AI to detect 'dark ships' by spotting AIS gaps that don't match radar or satellite images.

punchline.text: Every ship on Earth broadcasts its location—unless it's hiding.

quiz.question: What does AIS broadcast?
options: Ship identity, position, speed, and heading
